messages:
Alex: Heads up — cluster-autoscaler scaled down 2 nodes in gpu-pool-1 around 2026-03-16T18:12Z. One node had two long-running training pods and they were force-evicted mid-epoch :facepalm: Link to logs: https://internal.logs/redwood/scale-down/1764312345
Priya: ugh. do you have the pod names/events? was it a graceful termination or immediate eviction?
Alex: Pod names: training-bert-9f7 (requests: nvidia.com/gpu=4) and training-resnet-3c2. Events show Received SIGTERM then PodEviction; terminationGracePeriodSeconds was 30s so they started checkpoint but got killed before finish.
Devon: 30s is tiny for checkpointing GPU jobs. Options: increase terminationGracePeriodSeconds, add preStop hook to block until checkpoint, or prevent scale-down via PDB/annotation for critical jobs. But PDBs can also block CA and cause wasted nodes if overused.
Maya: agree. we should avoid global PDBs for every job. proposal: a) create a specific PriorityClass for long-running GPU jobs b) recommend job submitters set annotation cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false" when they want guaranteed no eviction c) improve autoscaler heuristics for gpu-pool-1.
Devon: note: cluster-autoscaler treats pods with annotation safe-to-evict=false as non-evictable and will skip draining nodes with only those pods. That can prevent scale-down => tradeoff.
Priya: maybe a middle ground: a short-term cordon-and-drain runbook for manual/automated safe-drain that coordinates with job controller to trigger a checkpoint window before drain.
Alex: rough runbook idea: 1) cordon node 2) annotate node with "drain-in-progress: true" 3) send a k8s event / webhook to job controller to checkpoint and gracefully terminate (give it e.g. 10m) 4) wait for pods to terminate or for grace window to expire 5) kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=0 --timeout=15m 6) uncordon on failure. Pseudocode below.
Devon: +1. can we add a lightweight script we can run as a Job or via maintenance controller? snippet: 
```bash
# safe-drain.sh - run on control-plane or as GitOps job
NODE=$1
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl annotate node $NODE maintenance/redwood-drain="in-progress" --overwrite
# notify job-controller via k8s Event or webhook (implementation-specific)
# wait_for_checkpoint() { sleep 600; } # placeholder 10m
# attempt graceful drain
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=15m --force || { echo "drain failed, uncordoning"; kubectl uncordon $NODE; exit 1; }
# mark node for scale-down by autoscaler
```
Maya: also: update docs for job authors: set terminationGracePeriodSeconds >= 300 for GPU training, implement incremental checkpoints every N steps, and expose a /drain endpoint so controllers can trigger checkpoints.
Priya: about PDB example if we do want limited protection (but be careful):
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: training-critical-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: training
```
This will stop CA from evicting a pod if it would violate minAvailable. only apply to critical replicas, not singletons across entire cluster.
Alex: also proposing a PriorityClass so eviction/ preemption behaves sensibly: 
```yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: gpu-longrunning
value: 100000
globalDefault: false
description: "High priority for long-running GPU training jobs to avoid preemption"
```
But high priority doesn't prevent CA scale-down unless paired with PDB/annotation.
SRE-bot: [auto] scale-down event detected for node group gpu-pool-1 at 2026-03-16T18:12Z. nodes_removed: 2. alert: investigate if evictions impacted SLAs.
Devon: follow-ups: 1) draft safe-drain script (owner: devon) 2) recommend terminationGrace default for gpu jobs (owner: priya) 3) prototype webhook-based checkpoint trigger (owner: maya) 4) consider node-group CA tuning: increase scale-down-utilization-threshold for gpu pools (owner: alex).
Priya: I can take docs and job examples. Will PR changes to training job templates (add grace >=300 and optional drain hook).
Alex: thanks. let's not apply blanket PDBs. prioritize the drain orchestration + checkpoint route. Will post a short RFC in #eng-sre tomorrow and link this thread. :thumbsup:
Maya: sounds good. I'll start prototyping the webhook flow this week.
SRE-bot: [auto] reminder: follow-up tasks created in Asana for owners listed above.
